plan: [ This is a one-shot, independent private values, second-price auction with rational opponents. In such auctions, bidding your true value is a weakly dominant strategy: overbidding risks paying above value if you win; underbidding risks losing when winning would yield positive surplus. There’s no history to learn from in round 1 of 1, so no strategic signaling or learning applies. To maximize expected profit, bid exactly my value so I win whenever the highest competing bid is below 19 and pay that second-highest bid. ]

[ This is a private-values, independent-draw, second-price auction with rational opponents. In such auctions, bidding one’s true value is a weakly dominant strategy: it maximizes expected profit regardless of others’ strategies. Overbidding risks winning at a price exceeding my value; underbidding risks losing profitable wins. With 0.1 increments, bid exactly 44.0. No past rounds to update beliefs. Aim: win iff my value exceeds competitors’, paying their highest bid. ]

[ This is a sealed-bid second-price auction. In such auctions, bidding your true value is a weakly dominant strategy: it maximizes expected profit regardless of others’ strategies. Overbidding risks winning at a price above value; underbidding risks losing when winning would have been profitable. With rational opponents likely bidding their values and no relevant history (1 round), bid exactly my value: 43. ]
